youtube.aciklama: Many people with single-sided deafness also have tinnitus in the deaf ear; in 2008, Van de Heyning and colleagues reported that a cochlear implant reduced tinnitus in these people. For most people, tinnitus drops clearly while the implant is on, and in some the effect partly persists when it is switched off; but it should not be expected to disappear completely, and tinnitus alone is not considered a reason for an implant.

In single-sided deafness, the deaf ear often has tinnitus too.
For most people, tinnitus drops clearly while the implant is on.
In some, the effect partly persists when the implant is switched off.
But tinnitus should not be expected to disappear completely.
Tinnitus alone is not considered a reason for an implant.
